questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses and the possibility to learn a new language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find out what courses I was allowed to take. And the different offices didn´t communicate, so it took me a long time to registrer for the right courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn´t make it to the intro session. And afterwards there wasn´t much help to find. My coordinator didn´t reply on my emails for months and he was rarely in his office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It took us some time (I lived with my boyfriend). But eventually we found an apartment through ParisAttitude. I can recommend that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It´s nice to live in another area than close to campus, if you want to explore more of Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
As mentioned, it was really difficult to find out what courses I was allowed to registrer for. And often I had to go to different offices in different parts of town and stand in long lines before I could talk to the administration about registrering for a course. 
The most tricky part was that I didn´t understand that there were certain combinations of courses I couldn´t take within Geography. They had written me an email about it, but it was very technical and I didn´t understand it. The professor who wrote be the email was not to be found in an office, and the administration I talked to didn´t know about her rules, so they allowed be to registrer for the courses I took even though I wasn´t allowed according to the professor who send me the email. It was partly my fault since I didn´t understand everything in the email. However my critique of the administration is that they gave me different information because they didn´t know of the same rules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the Erasmus-coordinator was almost impossible to reach. He didn´t reply for over a month and wasn´t in his office in his office hours. (He only had one office hour per week, and he wasn´t there two weeks in a row when I searched for him).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I managed to find some courses that were approved by my home university as well - thanks to my many free elective courses in my study program. But I had to give up on the courses in Geography that I had originally planed to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. Read the emails carefully. Don´t expect much help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I followed some very interesting courses and has some great teachers. I found it confusing, though, that I had to take so many courses for a small amount of ECTS.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses from first year of bachelor to master-level courses. They were all great. I found a couple of courses in english on master level in the program Philosophy of Science. The master courses were of course much more difficult than the ones in the bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general the courses consisted mostly of lectures. Very little, if any group work. Often no power points. Closed book, hand written exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Chimie et Société, Philosophie des Sciences, Bioéthique, Francais B2, Démocratie et Écologie, Darwinism and Metaphysics, Philosophy of Medicine, Travaille Personnelle.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Chimie et Société if you want the possibility to take the course online and in your own speed, there is a lot of work though. Philosophie des Sciences on first year of bachelor if you want and easy course (although it can also be time consuming) with power point. Démocratie et Écologie, Darwinism and Metaphysics and Philosophy of Medicine were all really interesting with very competent teachers. Bioéthique is difficult to understand in french because there is no power point, but the exam is not too hard.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Non. It is overall an expensive city and most of the social life takes place in the cafés, bars and restaurants.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wasn´t aware that there was an offer to do sport at my host institution before it was too late to sign up.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different kind of sport.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Museums and parcs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont and canal St Martin - follow it all the way up north.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is a nice culture with a lively atmosphere outside especially in the springtime and summer.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take a language course. If you have time, then do an intensive language course before the semester begins. It is a good way to meet international people. I found it difficult to become friends with french people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language, it is difficult to meet and become friends with french people. And there isn´t any long breaks during the courses to chat with the other students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Also the language. Even though it makes it more difficult to meet locals, it is a lovely language and a good way to become better at french is to do a semester at Sorbonne. And then I loved the lively culture of the cafés.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the administration. Take a french course and mingle with the internationals. Go to events by the university if you hear of anything - I heard about it through the students on the third year of the bachelor - there are whatsapp groups for the different programs - try to find students to add you to that and tell you about events.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have quite a long time after the semester has started to attend different courses and registrer for the ones you like the most. You don´t have to decide it all in advance.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I became much better at french and that I had some very interesting courses with good professors.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of exams. You have to take a lot of courses and there are often more exams in one course.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
